newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy December CPI at prelim 2.5/2.6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Italy December CPI at prelim 2.5/2.6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Italian consumer prices were running at 2.5-2.6 percent year on year and 0.05-0.1 percent month on month, according to analysts' estimates based on preliminary data from 10 sample cities.
Inflation grew at 2.6 percent in November year on year and at 0.3 percent month on month.
Analysts had forecast a year-on-year rate of 2.6 percent and and a monthly gain of 0.1 percent after the first four of the 10 cities released their data on Thursday.
The 10 cities have a combined weighting of 69.67 percent on the national index. The final CPI figures will be published by national statistics institute ISTAT on January 8.

Analysts surveyed before the last six cities released their data on Friday said a rate of 2.6 percent year on year meant there was scope for the Bank of Italy to lower its 7.5 percent discount rate as early as Friday evening or by Monday.

Seven economists polled by Reuters said they expected a rate cut, if it came, to be of the order of 50 or 50/75 basis points, with some saying a half point cut was more likely due to an impasse in wage negotiations between metalworkers and employers.
Metalworkers' unions announced on Thursday the pay talks with employers' association Federmeccanica had collapsed.
Unions were expecting a reply from the government later on Friday to their request that Rome step in formally to mediate in the dispute.

The Bank of Italy announced its last interest rate cut on October 23, when it lower the discount rate 75 basis points and the Lombard or fixed term advances rate 75 basis points to 9.0 percent. --Milan bureau +392 66129507
